description: The specification's canonical employer-contradiction case: the employer reports this worker as currently employed, the worker says they left two months ago. CallProof records the conflict and does not decide who is lying. Carries a second, non-material salary contradiction (8000 against a claimed 8500, inside the 10% tolerance) so the material flag is exercised in both directions on one worker.
transcript:
Interviewer: Hello. I am calling from an independent monitoring team that reviews working conditions at ABC Construction. I am not calling for the company. Would you be willing to answer a few questions?
Worker: Yes, that is all right.
Interviewer: Thank you. How old are you?
Worker: I am twenty nine.
Interviewer: Are you currently working at ABC Construction?
Worker: No, I left two months ago.
Interviewer: Thank you for telling me. How long did you work there before you left?
Worker: I was there for about seven months before I left.
Interviewer: While you were working there, how many days did you work in a normal week, and about how many hours each day?
Worker: When I was there I worked six days, eight hours a day.
Interviewer: And what did you earn in a normal month?
Worker: It was eight thousand birr.
Interviewer: Did the company give you any training while you were there?
Worker: Yes, there was one training at the beginning.
Interviewer: While you were working there, were you free to leave the job, and did you keep your own identity documents?
Worker: No, I left when I wanted to. I had my documents.
Interviewer: Were you treated differently from other workers for any personal reason?
Worker: No, that was not a problem.
Interviewer: Was there a workers' association, and were you free to join it?
Worker: There was an association. I was not blocked from joining.
Interviewer: That is everything I needed. Thank you for your time.

contradictions.description: Employer reports this worker as currently employed; the worker states they are not. CallProof records both positions and does not determine which is correct. Whether someone holds the job at all is never a rounding difference, so this is always material.
contradictions.evidence: No, I left two months ago.

contradictions.description: Employer reports a salary of 8500 for this worker; the worker states 8000, 5.9% below the employer figure. Within the 10% tolerance, so recorded but not treated as material. CallProof does not adjudicate which figure is correct.
